LLM_description:
Situation:
A severe cyclone has disrupted ground lines of communication across the river valley and coastal belt. Landslides, flooding, and debris have constrained access to a few viable corridors that require daily route clearance and armed escort. Three functioning supply nodes—Supply Depot Alpha (port district), Supply Depot Bravo (inland logistics hub), and Supply Depot Charlie (airhead)—hold limited, time-phased stocks of life-sustaining commodities (potable water, emergency rations, medical kits). Priority receiving nodes are the 1st Field Hospital, the 3rd Relief Battalion Distribution Hub, and IDP Camp Delta. The immediate lifesaving window is the next two operational periods (Day 1 and Day 2). The fleet consists of general cargo trucks with uniform capacity; vehicle availability is limited.

Mission:
Move prioritized commodities from Depots Alpha, Bravo, and Charlie to the three supported sites over two days to cover critical needs while minimizing total operational cost—balancing per-route transport costs, vehicle deployment costs, fixed route security risk costs, and penalties for any authorized shortfalls—within depot release limits, vehicle capacity, and total fleet availability.

Execution/Concept:
- Allocation and time-phasing: Do not dispatch more than each depot’s available supply on each day. Stocks are time-phased and cannot be overdrawn.
- Demand coverage: Aim to meet daily requirements at each supported site. If unavoidable, authorized shortfalls are permitted and will incur shortage penalties.
- Movement and capacity: Each truck has fixed payload capacity; commodity volumes differ and must be accounted for when loading. Shipments are planned by route and day.
- Route activation and security overhead: A route can only be used on a given day if it is activated. Activating a route (sending any vehicles) incurs a fixed Risk Cost for that day, representing escorts, route clearance, and security posture—this cost is incurred regardless of the number of vehicles assigned. Once active, vehicles may use the route subject to fleet limits.
- Fleet apportionment: The total number of vehicles assigned across all depot-to-unit routes on each day cannot exceed the available fleet. Each deployed vehicle incurs a deployment cost.
- Cost minimization: Consolidate flows onto fewer activated corridors where feasible to amortize fixed security overheads, while respecting depot release limits and truck capacity. Balance transport and vehicle costs against the penalties for unmet demand to prioritize life-saving deliveries (water and medical) on Day 1 and stabilize rations on Day 2.
- Priorities: Day 1—deliver potable water and medical kits to the 1st Field Hospital and IDP Camp Delta; position rations as feasible. Day 2—backfill remaining demands and redistribute as conditions permit.
- Coordination: The Movement Control Cell (JLCC) will issue a daily convoy tasking order, sequence loads at depots, and publish SP/RP times. Engineer teams will clear and certify activated corridors prior to convoy movement. Security escorts will be allocated to activated routes only. Receiving units will provide offload windows and confirm berth capacity.
